It happened exactly a week after that fruitless exchange.
这件事，发生在那次毫无结果的问答刚好一周后。

<I hereby confirm today’s close of business for the Sinners.>
<我批准罪人结束工作。>

Thank you kindly. Starting now, you all will be given a maximum of 12 hours to partake in sleep and rest; the duration is subject to change. Have a good night.
谢谢。从现在开始，你们最多有12个小时可供睡眠和休息，时间可能会有所变动。祝各位有个美好的夜晚。

Faust gives the same instructions as always. In response, Sinners groan and stretch like usual.
浮士德一如既往给出相同的指示。像往常那样，罪人们也纷纷伸着懒腰，呻吟着回应。

Except this time, one Sinner stuck out of that normalcy like a sore thumb.
不过这次，有一名罪人像是凸出的肿瘤般一反常态。

…What now?
……这次又怎么了？

Leave him be, Ishy~ It’s not the first time he’s all grumpy like that, is it?
没事啦，以实~他这样闹别扭又不是一天两天了，对吧？

And Heath~ Make sure to simmer down before you get in your room, ‘kay? All that grumbling thunder in there keeps me awake, y’know~
希斯~你可一定要消了气再回房间，好吗？我每次都被你房间里传来轰隆隆的打雷声吵得睡不着觉呢~

…The Sinners’ rooms—their lodging, personal space, and cell—reflect their state of mind, or so I’ve heard.
……罪人们的房间，也是他们的住所、私人空间与牢房，据说能够反映出他们的心象。

Each room’s floors, walls, and overall ambiance are shaped after the Sinner’s personality, and the view through the window changes depending on their emotions and mental state.
每个房间的地板、壁纸以及整体氛围都是根据罪人的个性塑造而成的，而透过另一面墙上的窗户看到的景色，貌似也会根据他们的心象和情感而产生不同的变化。

Though, all I’ve seen were distant glimpses through the window, so I don’t have all the details.
话虽如此，我所能见到的一切也不过是远远透过窗户看到的那一小部分，所以并不清楚所有的细节。

…The room Heathcliff enters would sometimes­—actually, rather frequently—emit wuthering and stormy sounds.
……希斯克利夫所进入的房间有时会——实际上，是相当频繁地，发出雷电与风暴交织的呼啸声。

…Tch.
……嘁。

Usually, he’d snap back with a “Why should I?” or something like that, but he only clicked his tongue.
通常会用“我凭啥那么干？”之类的话来回击的希斯克利夫，现在只是咂了咂嘴。

I suppose he doesn’t feel like arguing.
我猜是他不想争论了。

Thanks to that, he stood in the corridor until all the other Sinners (save for Faust) went into their rooms, staring down the passage with a frown. Maybe he was relieving stress this way.
幸亏如此，他就这么站着不动，皱着眉头凝视着走廊，直到所有其他罪人（准确来说除了浮士德）都走进他们的房间。也许他是在用这种方式来缓解压力吧。

…Oho?
……哦嚯？

And that right there is where the incident began.
而这，也成为了此次事件的导火索。

…Huh? Oi, what’s with all those doors down the aisle?
……嗯？喂，这么看来远处那边也有很多门？

Heathcliff pointed in the same exact direction I did a week ago.
希斯克利夫所指的方向与我一周前所指的完全相同。

Those doorways were beyond the “no trespassing” line blocking the way.
那些门伫立在“禁止越界”的封锁线之后。

Heathcliff, I recommend against walking farther into the corridor than necessary.
希斯克利夫，我建议你不要越过走廊的必要活动范围。

Huh. That sure makes it sound awful suspicious.
哈，这话听起来就更可疑了。

There is nothing of which to be suspicious. You are better off listening to Faust.
那没什么可疑的东西。你最好听浮士德的话。

What, you keep treasures or somesuch in there?
咋，你是把宝藏之类的东西藏在里面了？

Faust’s secretive attitude was enough to rouse his curiosity…
浮士德无可奉告的态度足以激起他的好奇心……

Heathcliff. Do not do it. You will regret your action.
希斯克利夫，不要那么做，你会为此后悔的。

…Got well emotional and gobby, eh, Ms. Cleveress?
……眨眼间变得情绪化了很多嘛，万事通小姐。

It’s like… you’re actually hiding something there!
就好像……你确实在那里藏着什么东西！

He sprinted into the dark before we could stop him.
我们还没来得及阻止，他就一头扎进了黑暗之中。

<What’s in there—>
<那里面……>

Just as I was about to ask Faust an obvious thing to be concerned over…
正当我要理所当然地向浮士德询问时……

GAAAAAAARGH?!!
咕啊啊啊啊啊啊啊？！！

Heathcliff’s sharp scream echoed from the unlit area far into the corridor.
希斯克利夫的惨叫声从漆黑的走廊深处传来。

Dante, now is the time to take my left hand and run with me.
但丁，从现在起请抓住我的左手，然后和我一同跑起来。

<Wha, huh?>
<嗯、嗯？>

I won’t be able to get him out in time on my own. I may be engulfed myself if I don’t act quickly.
我一个人没法及时把他拉出来。如果速度不够快的话，就连我自己也会被吞噬的。

Before I could process what she meant, Faust ran off in the direction Heathcliff disappeared.
在我理解她所说的话之前，浮士德就已经朝着希斯克利夫消失的方向跑去。

<Ah… Shuckaroonies! W—Wait for me!>
<啊……妈的！一、一起走啊！>

As we crossed the line and proceeded deeper into the corridor, we came across a three-way crossroads.
我们跨过了那条线，并沿着走廊不断深入，很快就来到了一处三岔路口。

<I think I heard screams coming from the middle…>
<好像从中间方向传来了悲鸣……>

However, without a moment’s hesitation, Faust darted for the left aisle.
但是，没有丝毫的犹豫，浮士德牵着我的手冲进了左边的走廊。

<F—Faust! I know you’re in a hurry, but… are you sure this is the right way? I could’ve sworn I heard his voice coming from the center path…>
<浮、浮士德！我知道很急……但不该是这条路吗？刚才是在中间这条路上听到了希斯克利夫的声音……>

I know.
我知道。

Without elaborating further, Faust continued running.
也不知道她知道了什么，浮士德只是默默地奔跑着。

At another fork we encountered, Faust chose the right path.
在下一个岔路口，浮士德选择了右边。

Right afterward, she entered the fifth door on the left side of that hallway.
紧接着，她便进入了那条走廊左侧的第五扇门。

<What… is this?>
<这是……什么啊？>

Right as I entered, another hall came into view.
就在我进去的时候，另一条走廊映入眼帘。

Its end… was like a cliff.
它的尽头……如同一座悬崖。

To be more precise, I felt some kind of gravitational pull trying to get me to fall to the end of the hallway.
更准确地说，我能感受到某种引力，正尝试将我们拖入走廊尽头的深渊。

<Heathcliff!!>
<希斯克利夫！！>

Then I saw him; he crawled toward us with all his might from the middle of the hall.
然后我看到了他，他在走廊中央用尽全力向我们爬来。

As if he might fall the moment he lets go…
就好像他松手的那一刻就会坠落下去……

What… the hell is all this… and this place…!
什么……这都他妈什么东西……还有这个地方……！

Even though I couldn’t see much in the dark behind him, I definitely felt some presence in it.
尽管看不见任何东西，但是我感觉到希斯克利夫身后的黑暗中分明有什么东西存在。

<Faust, what’s over—>
<浮士德，那后面的是……>

Dante, I want you to hold the knob of this open door tightly. Firmly grip my hand as well.
但丁，请紧紧握住这扇门的把手。也请您紧紧抓住我的手。

Holding my hand securely, she gradually approaches Heathcliff.
浮士德紧紧地抓着我的手，慢慢靠近了希斯克利夫。

<This hallway… isn’t tilted or anything, is it? Why does it feel like we’re hanging off a cliff?>
<这走廊……是没有倾斜的，没错吧？到底为什么会有一种被挂在悬崖上的感觉啊？>

That… is because we’re in a ‘corridor’, obviously. Dante, do not let go.
那……显然是因为我们在“走廊”里。但丁，不要松手。

Reminding me to hold fast, Faust extended her other arm while holding her zweihander.
浮士德如此回答道，并用另一只手抽出了双手剑。

Heathcliff, grab this if you would.
希斯克利夫，请抓住这个。

Are you mental?! My hand’ll get gashed if I try grabbing that giant blade!
你疯了吗？！要我抓上去的话，我的手会被那把大剑给割断的！

…You’ll much prefer deep wounds on your palms to what you can suffer down there.
……比起你将在那下面遭受的痛苦，你会更喜欢手掌上的深伤口的。

Baffled, Heathcliff looked at the sword and then the darkness behind him…
在错愕之中，希斯克利夫看了看那把剑，接着又看了看他身后的黑暗……

Bugger… Kgh, gaaahg…!
妈的……咳、咕啊啊……！

Dante, pull him up. Might and main.
但丁，请您全力拖拽。

<…G—Got it!>
<……好、好的！>

Grrgh, knngh…
呃呃，咳呃呃……

<Huff, hoogh…>
<哈、哈啊……>

Right as we pulled Heathcliff up…
就在我们把希斯克利夫拉上来的时候……

No, I’m not sure if it’s even right to say that we pulled him “up”, but nevertheless… Faust hoisted his unconscious body by the legs and started rushing, saying that we need to return the way we came.
不，我甚至不确定我们把他“拉上来”的说法是否准确，但尽管如此……浮士德说我们需要沿着来时的路回去，还没来得及问她什么，她便提起希斯克利夫的双腿，抬着他已失去知觉的身体跑了起来。

Following her lead, I supported his arms and trailed behind, keeping his head from dragging along the floor.
我也配合着她。由她领路，我支着希斯克利夫的胳膊跟在后面，防止他的头被拖在地板上。

After burning some time…
过了一段时间……

…Phew. Let us say that it is fortunate he wasn’t lost in a deeper area.
……呼。他在更深处迷失方向之前就变成了这样，应该说是不幸中的万幸。

Dante, you will have to turn the clock.
但丁，得请您转动时钟了。

<Heathcliff’s… gonna be okay, right?>
<希斯克利夫……他没事吧？>

The psychological damage is likely to be severe. Our work will be encumbered if he loses his mind.
应该会有很严重的精神损伤。就这样疯掉的话会对业务造成较大阻碍。

<Sigh…>
<哈……>

I didn’t have a choice.
我别无选择。

Good work back there, Dante. While it is unfortunate that we have lost a portion of our limited break time to this…
辛苦了，但丁。我为因此缩短那本不充裕的休息时间而感到可惜……

<Faust. Just what’s in there? Where does it lead?>
<浮士德。那里面到底有什么？又通向哪里？>

<Can’t you tell me at this point? I’ve… seen that stuff now.>
<现在总该告诉我了吧？毕竟都……见到了那种东西。>

It was only natural that I want to know. What resides there, and what was chasing Heathcliff?
这是理所当然的疑问。到底是什么东西在那里面，希斯克利夫又是被什么东西所追逐。

Moreover…
还有……

Why did it never show itself to us, and why did it vanish instead of chasing him any further?
为什么那东西既没有向我们露出真面目，也没有追到希斯克利夫就直接消失了。

These questions were driving me crazy, but alas…
虽然我好奇到快要疯了……

As stated earlier, there are limits to what Faust can elaborate.
就如我一开始所说，浮士德所能说的事情是有所限制的。

…Yep, I honestly didn’t expect much.
……没错，说实话我并没有期待什么。

The corridor, you I.F.
走廊。懂·自·懂。

Ryōshū muttered with a cigarette in her mouth, walking past us both. She must’ve left her room while we were out on our rescue mission.
良秀嘴里叼着一支香烟，从我与浮士德两人之间走过。她一定是在我们执行救援任务时离开房间的。

However…
但是。

Faust proceeded as if not a soul had just walked by, as if nothing was just said.
浮士德就像刚刚无人经过也无事发生一般继续说道。

<Huh?>
<啊？>

You did prevent a sudden vacancy in the bus department.
鉴于您成功阻止了将会导致巴士部门产生空位的突发情况。

Though I wouldn’t exactly call it a reward, I do suppose it isn’t a bad idea to inform you of one thing.
虽然……说不上是奖励，但我觉得为了今后的事情着想，告诉您一两件事倒也不坏。

<Ooh… L-Lemme hear it!>
<哦哦……可、可以！>

The unexpected boon had me rubbing my hands together. Right, what will she tell me now…
意料之外的进展让我不禁搓起手来。好了，这下她会说些什么……

…Dante, when you traverse a road you have never walked before, what do you do?
……但丁，在寻觅一条未曾踏足过的路时，您会怎么做呢？

<Hmm? I mean… You use a map, obviously?>
<嗯？那当然是……翻开地图找路吧？>

That’s right. Then, even if you don’t have a map, your brain will form images to serve as one.
是的。以及就算没有地图，您的脑中也会产生类似于地图的表象。

From there, on that map… there will be a starting point and a destination clearly marked. When you return from your trip, you will trace back through that way.
如此一来，地图之中……就会存在确切的起点与终点。在返回时，您就会摸索着这些进行返程。

It’s so obvious, I don’t need to verbally answer. I just nodded along.
这是无需回答的理所当然之事。我只点了点头。

…Hopefully that makes it clear enough.
……希望这样的回答能让事情变得足够明了。

<Huh?>
<嗯？>

This is why you should remember where you’ve started in the corridor, especially when you open a door.
因此，尤其是当你打开一扇门的时候，你应当牢记你在走廊中的起始位置。

Flabbergasted by the abrupt end, I blurted.
突然结束的解释让我目瞪口呆，我突然想要说些什么。

Now then, Faust has grown tired. Do take care…
现在，浮士德已经累了。那就此告辞……

She walked through the door before I could say something, leaving me with a riddle.
但我还没来得及说出嘴边的话，她就走进门内，只给我剩下一个谜团。

<Of course it would go like this…>
<就知道会这样……>

I sighed out of frustration, but not a breath of air is expelled from my pitiful clock.
我沮丧地叹了口气，但这可悲的时钟却无法卷起一点微风。

Still, left powerless…
一如既往，我还是无能为力……

All I can do is boot up this electronic notebook and piece together what little information I have collected.
我所能做的就是启动这个电子笔记本，把我收集的这些信息碎片拼凑记录起来。
